sources.edition: John O'Donovan English edition; 17th c compilation, 19th c translation

sources.work: Royal Irish Academy Dictionary of Irish Biography on Niall O'Neill

sequences.actor: Gerald FitzGerald of Kildare and military coalition
sequences.claim: Kildare marched into Carrickfergus and destroyed Belfast castle; appointed a local military administrator at Carrickfergus.
sequences.not_automatic_proof: No proven countywide permanent English Crown administration

sequences.actor: Niall son of Con O'Neill and local Gaelic forces
sequences.basis: Four Masters M1507.13 AND Ulster U1507.6; DIB Niall Mór O'Neill
sequences.claim: Niall O'Neill captured the great castle of Carrickfergus, including town mayor / held hostages, after earlier imprisonment and release.
sequences.not_automatic_proof: Neither all town government nor County Antrim automatically changed long-term sovereignty

sequences.claim: O'Donnell force took Enniskillen fortress and handed it to a Maguire ally, showing inter-Gaelic rights and offices.
sequences.not_automatic_proof: Not Crown of England castle; exact building/location/reign dates require archaeological/historical corroboration

sequences.actor: Gerald FitzGerald Earl of Kildare / sons of Con O'Neill
sequences.basis: Four Masters M1509.4 AND Ulster U1509.8
sequences.claim: O'Neill allied faction seized Dungannon before Kildare arrived; Kildare took Omagh and demolished it, then returned home.
sequences.not_automatic_proof: English deputy's army not remaining after demolition; do NOT show Omagh as permanent 1509–1510 English-controlled city or district

sequences.claim: 1512 annal reports O'Donnell rebuilt in a week the Omagh castle earlier demolished by Kildare in 1509, and left his own garrison.
sequences.not_automatic_proof: Later adjacent decade event is a retrospective crosscheck of 1509 destruction, NOT a 1509 occurrence.

reliability_cautions: Annals of Ulster and Four Masters are different compilations, but may share historiographical traditions; do not call fully independent eyewitness reports.
Written modern line identifications for Gaelic castles require separate historical-archaeological concordance.
A castle attack is neither a complete map of political sovereignty nor reliable continuous full-decade legal rule.
1512 Omagh rebuild reference supports that 1509 Kildare demolition occurred but does not independently prove the timing of 1509 occupation to the day.
